Let's just explain. Are you familiar with Lajkovac and Ljig? Do these names ring any bells?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know that they're in the vicinity of Valjevo?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: I know that is there Irig close to us. I don't know about any other.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to our information, those places are in the general area of Valjevo. Further on, it says: My task as commander, as the TO commander of the 4th Operations Zone, was to carry out mobilisation, to train people, to bring the unit into the sector, to the command post of the 2nd Infantry Motorised Brigade in Tovarnik. And I was supposed to hand over the unit to the brigade commander. Do you know whether, at the time, there was indeed a JNA unit in the area; and, if there was, what unit was that?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: I don't know. They didn't tell us. I only know that the military post was 4795, because documents were stamped with that stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And later, he says the later fate of the unit and their engagement depended on the plan of the commander of the 2nd Infantry Motorised Brigade. It says the brigade commander decided that the anti-sabotage detachment should be sent to the Cakovci village and the Ljig Territorial Defence company and the Lajkovac Territorial Defence company should be sent to the village of Lovas. On that very same day, members of the Ljig TO company and the members of the anti-sabotage detachment transferred to Lovas or Cakovci, and the TO from Lajkovci, on the following day in the morning, moved to Lovas. And then he says that, together with the members of the Ljig TO company, he went to Lovas and assisted the company commander. He mentions his name. He assisted in deploying the unit in the village and then returned to Tovarnik and reported to the commander of the 2nd Infantry Brigade and continued to Valjevo. Were you aware of this information about these units that were, in fact, in Lovas? That's what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now this brings us to the incident that occurred. It says that: About seven days later, I took some of the TO units from the 4th Operations Zone to rotate in the territory of Eastern Slavonia. And on that occasion, I visited my units in the village of Cakovci and in the village of Lovas. I arrived in Lovas in the evening and I established contact with Lieutenant-Colonel Dimitrijevic from the Valjevo TO staff. Does this name mean anything to you? Lieutenant-Colonel Dimitrijevic.

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: No, it's the first time I've heard the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You saw some active-duty JNA officers and active-duty TO officers in Lovas when you were there.

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. The only name that I know is Marko Kovac. That is the only name of an officer that I, in fact, know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, does that mean that you don't know of any others, of any other officers? Does that mean that there were no such officers or that they were present but you did not know their names?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: I did not know their names because a lot of them arrived and passed through, and these were people I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The person who gave the statement then says that: On that occasion, Dimitrijevic complained to me because snipers were opening fire on them at night from the direction of the Jelas forest. My question is, once again, whether you heard -- I don't mean from this officer, but whether you heard from the members, from the local Serbs or from members of the Territorial Defence or from someone else that they had this problem with snipers.

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: No, I heard nothing about it. We were in our houses at night. We couldn't move around. You could hear shooting, but this was mostly in the village itself. And they didn't provide us with any information. They didn't tell us that someone was opening fire on them or anything of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And could you please tell me something else: Where is that Jelas forest located in relation to the clover field, which is where you were taken to later?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: It's about a kilometre and a half to 2 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that if you were going from Lovas towards the Jelas forest you would pass by this field on your way there?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: He goes onto say that he told that officer that no action to search the field was to be taken without the authorisation of the commander of the 2nd Infantry Motorised Brigade, but some Captain Markovic reacted and said that some sort of action should be taken. Have you heard of that name?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: No, I haven't. The only name I know is Marko Kovac. The only officer's name I know is Marko Kovac. As for the other officers, I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: He then says that he provided Devetak with information, that he hadn't been spoken to. He went to see the company commander of the Ljig TO. And when he went to Lovas on the 21st of October, 1991, that was the next time he went there, so that the Valjevo TO could be rotated, he was then informed about locals who had been killed in the village, in the minefield, and he was told that the entire procedure was under the authority of the security organs of the 2nd Guards Infantry Motorised Brigade and the 1st Guards Infantry Battalion. What I'm interested in is: When this happened, after the event, did anyone from those organs who were supposed to be involved in this procedure to determine what had happened in the minefield, did anyone from those organs speak to the locals from Lovas, to the local Croats from Lovas, to some of those, in fact, who had been taken to the minefield and who had been wounded or who, in fact, hadn't been wounded there?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no one spoke to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is his Official Note on the report. [In English] At this moment I would tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification is the proposal, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I spoke to counsel originally and I had said that on principle I didn't have any objections to it being tendered. However, I'm afraid this is not the right witness. He has said the first paragraphs contains wrong information, and in all the paragraphs after that, he said that he can't confirm anything, not the names, not the information. So I don't think this witness has laid a sufficient foundation for it to be admitted. But I don't have a problem with it being MFI'd for later use with a proper witness, but the MFI status would not be on the basis of a lack of translation, in my view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I don't think we would MFI pending another witness if -- if -- if there is no nexus between this witness and the document. There is another solution, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: There is no nexus between this witness and the witness who provided this information, but there is a close nexus between testimony of this witness and information provided by this person.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Again, I can only refer to the record. The first paragraph was read to the witness, and he said the information about them being there to prevent certain crimes is absolutely wrong and that they did the opposite. He was asked about the information provided in this document about Tovarnik. He said he didn't know. He was asked about this -- I'm sorry, my Cyrillic is -- Dimitrijevic or -- that name. He said he wasn't familiar with that person. In the next paragraph about Jelas, he was asked if he was familiar with the sniper firing. He said he didn't. And that that continued. He confirmed nothing in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, the document fails -- fails nexus, and it will not be admitted through this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that the witness -- that's your decision, okay. I will not comment. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your statement, you said that 70 locals went from Lovas to Ilok. Well, today, in fact, you said 60. But that's not the point of my question. But I noticed that, amongst other things, you said that prior to the meeting -- in fact, could you have a look at your statement. It's the second paragraph. It says that an officer -- or, rather, it says that an ultimatum was issued to the local inhabitants of Lovas, and it says it was decided not to mount any resistance because that would have been ineffective. And in the second paragraph you say: I mustn't forget to say that immediately prior to the meeting of the local inhabitants, one day earlier several Croatian policemen from Ilok came to the village and they collected the Kalashnikovs, a few Kalashnikovs that we had, and they took them to Ilok.

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us something about these Kalashnikovs. What do you know about them?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: I didn't see them, but I know that people said that the police arrived and they took several Kalashnikovs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did they take them from anyone?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: I don't know. All they said is that they appeared and left with those Kalashnikovs. I assumed that the Kalashnikovs were in the municipality building because of the guards that were being mounted. I didn't see them. As I said, I had a hunting rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that there were others who would mount guard and who had these Kalashnikovs on them?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, would this be an appropriate time?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, we will take the second break. We will have to take that because of earlier commitments during the break. We will be back at 12.45. You will be escorted out of the courtroom now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll now put a few questions to you about the incident in the minefield. And, to be more specific, about the time when the first mine was activated. In your statement, you said the following -- in the Croatian version it's on page 6, paragraph 3. You said that after you had covered about 10 metres, someone cried out and said that he had seen a wire and then an explosion was heard. What I would like know is whether you could tell us, how much time passed between the point when someone said that he saw a wire until the time that the explosion was heard?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Perhaps a second or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- page 6, paragraph 3 of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Of B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: B/C/S of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Of -- of the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Can we have it on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just, Your Honour, I tell you what is the paragraph in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Excuse me, is it the 1996 statement to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: 1996 statement -- statement is dated the 6th and 7th February 1996. It is --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: It's 65 ter number --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: 243 -- or 213. I cannot read properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: It's tab 14, I believe, from the Prosecution, and it's 65 ter number 3253, if that assists.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think it ... Yes, we have it on the screen. It is page -- it is page 6 in B/C/S, and ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So -- tab 9, 65 ter number 2236. Let's see if that's the one you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, do you have a precise purpose to go back to this statement? This is a viva voce witness. We do agree, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the statement I refer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to put the witness -- to -- to put some question related to the event of 18 of October to the witness. If it is not necessary, I will not do it -- do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well, it's up to know whether it is necessary or not. I'm just a little bit surprised by the fact that you go to a prior statement while the witness gave ample testimony about this in court. But go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we shouldn't use this statement, okay, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any event, you mentioned the time when the first mine was activated and what I'm interested in, irrespective of what you said in the statement, is how much time elapsed from the time when someone shouted out and said that he seen a mine until the point in time when the mine exploded, and I believe your answer was that it was a second or two.

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me how far you were from the place where the first mine was activated?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: About 10 to 15 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And here you say that Ivan Kraljevic accidentally activated the first mine.

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. That is what first occurred to me. At that point in time, that's what I thought, and I still believe that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have another question about the subsequent clearing of the minefield. I believe that you said that you received instructions, according to which, once you a noticed a wire, you -- to inform them of the fact and everyone were to lie down on the ground -- everyone had to lie down on the ground until the person who had spotted a mine managed to deactivate it.

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And that warning was issued by a soldier.

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. One of those who were up there on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Once the mines were disarmed, you went up to the road. I believe that that was done according to the instructions. Once you disarmed the mines, you were supposed to bring them up to the roads, to the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see that the clover at some places in the field, did you see that from the position on the road? Did you see that the clover was trampled on?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, you could see four tracks where the lines had been laid. The road was about 3 or 4 metres above the field, and you could see clearly that somebody had walked through the field and left their traces in the form of four lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you were walking through the clover field and you said that the clovers were about 30 centimetres high, did you not see the same thing, that the clovers were trampled on at places?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Only when we arrived and when the first mine went off, we saw the passages through the clover field, we saw the thin wires. It was only then that it dawned on us that the field had been mined.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And then you drew a logical conclusion that there were other places where the clovers were trampled on, where mines had been laid.

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And let me put just one more question to you. It concerns the part of your statement in which you stated that you were walking in the direction of the minefield, escorted by soldiers, and that you acted as human shields for those soldiers.

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And that continued until you reached the clover field.

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And, later on, when you reached the clover field, what happened to the soldiers? Were they still with you? Did they go elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: They remained standing on the road. We were spread. We turned right. They remained on the road. They made us face the forest. One group came after us, some ten or 15 of them, and the others remained standing on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that they made you face the forest, are you talking about the forest called Jelas?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: They -- we did not face the forest because the forest was about 1 to 1 and a half kilometres away from the minefield, but they were facing that direction, the direction of the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But was it Jelas forest?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Jelas forest is about a kilometre and a half from the minefield so we could not see the forest because it was in a depression. We couldn't see it. We just faced that direction, the direction of the administrative building of the agricultural co-operative.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to make sure that we're talking about that forest or some other forest.

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: No. Jelas forest is about a kilometre and a half away from that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just one -- one more time. Let's clarify this. Although the forest was about a kilometre or a kilometre and a half away from the minefield, it was still Jelas forest; right?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And just one more thing, and I believe that it is going to be my last question. Those soldiers that remained behind you once you reached the clover field and when they made you face the clover field with Jelas forest in the distance, where were those soldiers? Not the ones on the road but the others.

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: They were behind our backs, some ten to 15 metres behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In practical terms, you were no longer acting as their human shield; right?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: We were in front of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At a distance of some ten to 15 metres?

utterances.speaker: GH-095 [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Anything in re-direct, Ms. Biersay?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, this time it's for real, this is the end of your testimony. You're now released as a witness and we wish you, once again, a safe journey back home. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Nothing else on the agenda?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Not on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Not on behalf of the Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 30th day of November, 2012, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.02 p.m.,
